The place, which is a major tourist hotspot, is now being transformed into a major tourism hub to conserve the region’s natural and cultural heritage. Here’s what we know about these plans so far. Bodh Gaya To Get A Major Eco-Tourism Boost According to The Times of India, authorities in Bihar are now focusing on developing the natural landscapes of Bodh Gaya and turning it into a major eco-tourism hub in the state. The Environment, Forest and Climate Change Department is considering developing Maya Sarovar, Muchalinda Sarovar, the Dungeshwari area and the surrounding beautiful hills as key sites for nature-based tourism. The initiative aims to promote sustainable tourism. The move will also ensure the conservation of the region’s natural and cultural heritage. Bodh Gaya in Bihar is one of the most sacred places in the world for Buddhists. Many people visit the place to pay their respects at the ancient Mahabodhi Temple. It has a water body, green landscapes and offers a laser show based on the life of Buddha. People often visit this place to soak in the tranquil and peaceful vibes. According to The Times of India, the department is planning more eco-tourism activities around other spots in Bodh Gaya. The focus will be on environmental protection, cleanliness and the involvement of local communities in tourism-related activities. There would be nature walks, trekking, bird watching, nature camps and eco-friendly accommodation for tourists. These plans may help to bring tourists closer to nature while also creating awareness about the need to protect the environment. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar floods affect over 40 lakh people across 14 districts
bihar_raw_news.content: Villagers inspect repair work following a breach in the Mahi river dam after a rise in the water level, at Parsa in Saran district, Bihar PTI National Bihar floods affect over 40 lakh people across 14 districts "Incessant rain in various districts caused rivers and streams to overflow. Besides, heavy rainfall in catchment areas of Nepal has also led to rivers flowing above the danger level at several places," an official said PTI Updated: 9th Sep, 2026 at 2:05 PM PATNA: More than 40 lakh people have been affected by floods across 14 districts of Bihar following torrential rains over the past five days, with several rivers flowing above the danger mark, officials said on Wednesday. "Incessant rain in various districts caused rivers and streams to overflow. Besides, heavy rainfall in catchment areas of Nepal has also led to rivers flowing above the danger level at several places," an official said. According to a statement by the Disaster Management Department (DMD), around 40.21 lakh people in 514 gram panchayats across 84 blocks in 14 districts have been affected by floods. The affected districts are Patna, Bhojpur, Saran, Vaishali, Bhagalpur, Begusarai, Buxar, Samastipur, Munger, Katihar, Lakhisarai, Khagaria, Purnia and Arwal. According to the meteorological service centre, the state has recorded 79.6 mm of rainfall in September so far, which is 31 per cent above normal. In its latest bulletin, the DMD said, "The Ganga at Sultanganj in Bhagalpur recorded 36.78 metres at 9 am on September 9, surpassing its previous Highest Flood Level (HFL) of 36.75 metres recorded on August 17, 2021. The trend, however, remains stable." Several rivers, including the Gandak, Kosi, Budhi Gandak, Ganga, Punpun, Bagmati and Ghaghra, are flowing above danger levels at multiple locations, officials said. The water levels of the Gandak at Dumariya Ghat, Kosi at Baltara and Kursela, Burhi Gandak at Khagaria, and Ganga at Digha, Gandhi Ghat, Hathidah, Bhagalpur and Kahalgaon, as well as at Munger, Punpun at Sripalpur, Bagmati at Benibad, and Ghaghara at Darauli and Gangpur Siswan, are flowing above the danger mark.

bihar_raw_news.content: Pappu Yadav raises alarm over Bihar floods, says 55 lakh people affected ANI | Updated: Sep 09, 2026 11:07 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 9 (ANI): Purnia MP Pappu Yadav on Wednesday raised concerns over the worsening flood situation in Bihar, claiming that around 55 lakh people across 22 districts are facing difficulties due to the floods. Yadav said the crisis has affected people across economic sections, with the lower middle class, middle class and poor all struggling to cope with the situation. He said the flood-affected belt stretches from Buxar to Manihari, while several parts of Bhagalpur, Patna, Begusarai and Munger are also partially inundated. Describing the situation in Patna as particularly serious, Yadav said only around 4-5 km of highland could be seen in the city. He said people were facing difficult conditions at various ghats, where women were sleeping on floors while animals remained surrounded by floodwater. “Whichever ghat you go, you’ll find women sleeping on floors, animals are in water, fodder has become wet,” Yadav said, highlighting the difficulties being faced by people who have been displaced or forced to stay in flood-hit areas. He also raised concerns over the quality of drinking water being supplied to affected people. Yadav alleged that the water being provided through tankers was of such poor quality that politicians themselves would not drink it. The Congress leader further claimed that essential supplies were becoming difficult to access in several flood-hit areas. According to him, children were not getting milk, medicines were unavailable, and some places were facing a complete lack of electricity. "The water in the tanker is so bad that none of the politicians would drink it. Children are not getting milk, medicines are unavailable," he added. “There isn’t a single candle. There’s no electricity,” Yadav said, pointing to the problems faced by people in areas where power supply has been disrupted. He also highlighted the impact of the floods on livestock and fodder. With animals standing in floodwater and fodder becoming wet, the crisis has extended beyond immediate shelter and food requirements, he said. Yadav’s remarks come as floodwaters have affected large parts of Bihar, with residents in several areas facing disruption to daily life and access to basic necessities. Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Tuesday detailed the government's response to intense flooding caused by sudden water surges upstream in Nepal and Tibet. Emphasising Bihar's geographical vulnerability as a lower riparian state, Chief Minister Choudhary highlighted both the immediate emergency measures deployed to protect lower riparian districts and long-term infrastructural DPRs (Detailed Project Reports) focused on river interlinking and dam construction. Speaking to ANI, Choudhary outlined immediate rescue operations and long-term river infrastructure projects designed to mitigate recurring inundations. "Look, there are continuous flood risks, and two major rivers are the primary source of flooding. There are also other rivers such as the Budhi Gandak, Bagmati, Kamala, and Mahananda. bihar_raw_news.title: Indian states step up Gulf investor push as UAE becomes gateway to global markets
bihar_raw_news.content: Agencies States race to woo Gulf investors as MP offers extra incentives to big-ticket projects Dubai: Several states in India are intensifying their pursuit of investments from the Gulf, with Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Bihar and Punjab reaching out to sovereign wealth funds , family offices, and companies in the UAE, offering a mix of customised incentives, industrial land, and sector-specific opportunities. These states are increasingly looking at the UAE not just as a source of investment but as a gateway to the entire Gulf and other global markets, pitching their manufacturing, agriculture, mining, logistics and technology capabilities to investors at an annual investment meeting in Dubai and through one-to-one meetings with sovereign investors and business groups. Also read: Indian Inc rushes to align with UAE’s 15% minimum tax as November deadline looms Madhya Pradesh chief minister Mohan Yadav told ET that the state is prepared to offer additional, customised incentives to large investors and wanted UAE companies to use the state as a production base for exports into the Gulf and beyond. "If someone wants to make a significantly large investment, I am willing to give further incentives through the Cabinet Committee for Investment Promotion (CCIP)," said Yadav, adding that the state is prepared to go "out of the way" to support companies bringing in significant investments. The CCIP is the state's top level mechanism for fast tracking large investments and can approve customised support for major industrial projects, including granting specific waivers, exemptions, or deferments on electricity duty, stamp duty, royalty, and government dues. Live Events ET Bureau Vie for gulf capital Notably, Odisha CM Mohan Charan Majhi has brought forward his UAE visit from December to September amid improving the geopolitical environment and growing activity among other Indian states and investors to attract Gulf capital, Odisha additional chief secretary Hemant Sharma told ET. During his three-day visit, Majhi is slated to meet with sovereign wealth funds, family offices, and prominent investment houses. Majhi's visit comes more than two months after Odisha secured a proposed $11.3 billion integrated aluminium project involving Abu Dhabi-based International Holding Co (IHC) and Adani Group for an aluminium project. "We were supposed to come here a little later this year, but we advanced the visit as the geopolitical situation has largely been resolved, so there is a rush of activity, and we didn't want to miss out on some of the prospective investment," said Sharma. Mineral-rich Odisha is particularly seeking investments in mining and metallurgy, chemicals and petrochemicals, and port-based logistics. "Besides, we are also focusing on new emerging sectors such as semiconductors and electronic data centres for drawing investments," he said. MP CM Yadav, who is in Dubai to meet investors and business groups, has held talks with representatives of companies including DP World, VFS Global, Emaar, Lulu Group, Choithrams, and business chambers besides seeking talks with sovereign wealth funds. national_raw_news.content: Praising the remarkable achievement of India’s rise in fintech, Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that the country’s Unified Payments Interface (UPI) is the undisputed champion of this success story. Inaugurating the ‘Global Fintech Fest 2026’ in Mumbai, Mr Modi said this is such a massive transformation that whenever fintech is discussed, it will remain incomplete without UPI. Reiterating his core philosophy of technological empowerment, the Prime Minister praised UPI as the ultimate tool for financial inclusion, successfully penetrating areas ignored by traditional banking models. The Prime Minister pointed out that over 24 billion UPI transactions occurred in August alone. Mr Modi said that because of this impact, French President Emmanuel Macron said that UPI is not just a tech story; it is a civilizational story. Highlighting the global expansion of India’s flagship digital payment system, Prime Minister said that UPI is now live in 11 countries, turning what was once unimaginable into an everyday reality for international payments. Outlining the next strategic phase for international digital payments, Mr Modi emphasised the urgent need to integrate UPI with the domestic payment systems of partner countries, mirroring the seamless cross-border connectivity already established with Singapore. He directed stakeholders to actively link financial networks wherever large Indian populations reside or extensive trade occurs. Emphasising the economic benefits for the diaspora, PM Modi pointed out that reducing transaction costs for the world’s largest remittance-sending population is a critical priority. He explained that integrating digital payment systems globally would significantly accelerate the transfer of funds to families back home.

national_raw_news.content: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has described Indian community in Sri Lanka as a bridge between the two countries, saying they play a crucial role in strengthening friendship between the two nations. Mr Singh, who reached Colombo yesterday on a three-day visit to Sri Lanka, made the remarks while interacting with members of the Indian diaspora. The Defence Minister said that India will always stand firmly with Sri Lanka in times of crisis, underlining that the relationship between the two countries is based on shared history, culture and faith. He said both nations share close cultural and civilisational ties, which have provided a strong foundation for the growth of the bilateral relationship. In his address, Mr Singh highlighted India’s rapid economic transformation, saying the country is among the fastest-growing major economies in the world and contributes more than 16 per cent to global growth. Noting that India’s economy grew at 7.8 per cent in the first quarter of 2026-27 amid global economic challenges, Mr. Singh pointed out that India has concluded trade deals with 38 countries over the last 12 years, including Free Trade Agreements (FTA) with eight major nations. Referring to the India-European Union FTA as the ‘Mother of All Deals’, he said the agreement opens access to the massive EU market and reflects India’s growing diplomatic and economic capabilities. Mr. Singh credited Prime Minister Narendra Modi for the significant rise in India’s global credibility, saying that compared to 12 years ago, the world today listens when India speaks on the international stage. Mr Singh, who is leading a high-level delegation comprising senior officials from the ministries of defence and external affairs, was received at the Bandaranaike International Airport by Sri Lanka’s Deputy Minister of Defence Maj Gen (Retd) Aruna Jayasekara.

national_raw_news.title: 6 hours ago | International 117 Canada Hits More Than 600 US Products with Tariffs Up to 50%
national_raw_news.content: Canada has imposed retaliatory tariffs of up to 50% on more than 600 US goods, escalating the trade dispute between two neighbours. The tariffs targeting US merchandise officially came into force last night. Canadian commercial enterprises are operating under the federal government’s newly implemented dollar-for-dollar tariffs, covering approximately 28 billion US dollars’ worth of American imports. The measures, which took effect at midnight, impose tariffs ranging from 15% to 50% on more than 600 US products. The affected goods include industrial materials such as steel and aluminium, household essentials such as toilet paper, and specialised products such as coin-operated arcade machines. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump has ordered federal agencies to stop purchasing Canadian products through the government’s primary procurement catalogue until Ottawa provides American businesses and farmers with equal access to the Canadian market. The directive instructs the General Services Administration (GSA) and the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) to immediately begin removing Canadian products from federal procurement channels. In a social media post, Trump accused Canada of unfair trade practices, alleging that Canadian federal and provincial governments prevent American small businesses from selling to public-sector entities while Canadian companies enjoy relatively open access to US government contracts.

national_raw_news.title: Indian Contingent for Asian Games 2026 Receives Grand Send-off in New Delhi 8 hours ago 128
national_raw_news.content: The Indian contingent for the Asian Games 2026 received a grand send-off in New Delhi yesterday in the presence of Youth Affairs and Sports Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya. Dr. Mandaviya, along with Indian Olympic Association President P T Usha, Sports Secretary Hari Ranjan Rao, and Chef de Mission Sahdev Yadav, unveiled the official jersey of the Indian contingent in the presence of athletes and support staff. Addressing the gathering, Dr. Mandaviya urged Indian athletes to turn pressure into performance, view opponents as opportunities and transform those opportunities into achievements. Highlighting Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision for Indian sports, he said the Government has created new pathways for athletes to compete and excel at the global level. Dr Mandaviya also highlighted the growing depth of Indian sport and the emergence of young talent. He said that out of the 503-member contingent, more than three hundred athletes are first-time participants at the Asian Games. Applauding India’s performance at the Commonwealth Games 2026 in Glasgow, the Union Minister said at the last Commonwealth Games, India won 13 gold medals and this time the tally has improved by more than 35 per cent. He said the target is to establish India firmly on the world sporting stage by 2036, when the country aims to host the Olympic Games. He added that this ten-year plan includes an allocation of more than 36 thousand crore rupees for improving sports infrastructure. The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports informed us that the Asian Games 2026 will be held in Japan, where the Indian contingent will compete across multiple sporting disciplines. The 503-member contingent includes athletes and support staff, with more than three hundred athletes set to make their debut at the Asian Games, reflecting the growing depth and bench strength of Indian sport.

national_raw_news.content: The 9th National Nutrition Month was inaugurated with great fanfare at the International Rudraksh Convention Center in Varanasi today. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, along with Union Minister for Women and Child Development Annapurna Devi, inaugurated the program by lighting a lamp in the presence of Minister of State for Women and Child Development Savitri Thakur and other ministers of the Uttar Pradesh government. Speaking on the occasion, Union Minister Annapurna Devi said that through the 9th National Nutrition Month, it’s a commitment to a well-nourished and empowered India. This campaign is linked to the health of every mother, the nutrition of every child, and the prosperity of every family. She said that pure and balanced nutrition is a strong foundation for a healthy and prosperous nation. On this occasion, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, nutrition for the poor, children, pregnant women, and lactating mothers has been prioritised since 2014. The Anganwadi centre system in Uttar Pradesh has also undergone significant changes. These centres are now becoming centres not just for nutrition distribution but for children’s health, nutrition, and early development. He said that the spirit of “Our Anganwadi, Our Responsibility” must be transformed into a campaign of public participation. The inaugural event in Varanasi featured a nutrition fair, a video presentation based on beneficiaries’ experiences, and a dialogue between the Union Minister and Anganwadi workers. Additionally, the Chief Minister gathered feedback from Anganwadi workers from across the country on their work and sought suggestions on how to improve it. He along with Union Minister also inspected the stalls set up for the occasion.

national_raw_news.title: Mizoram’s Saitual Becomes First District in State to Achieve ‘Surakshit’ HIV Status 2 hours ago 41
national_raw_news.content: North-eastern Mizoram’s Saitual, bordering Manipur, has become the only district in Mizoram to attain ‘Surakshit’ status under the National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO)’s Mobilisation AIDS Suraksha (MAS) campaign after achieving all three of the 95-95-95 HIV treatment and prevention targets. Under the UNAIDS-linked 95-95-95 targets, 95% of all people estimated to be living with HIV should know their status, 95% of those diagnosed should receive antiretroviral therapy (ART), and 95% of those on treatment should achieve viral load suppression. Districts under the MAS campaign are classified into four categories based on their performance: Sangharshee for those yet to achieve any of the three targets, Saksham for those meeting two, Surakshit for those achieving all three, and Surakshit+ for districts that also achieve zero mother-to-child transmission of HIV. The MAS campaign, launched in February, aims to break the chain of HIV transmission by achieving the 95-95-95 goals across the country. District-level progress is reviewed regularly under the leadership of deputy commissioners. According to the August report, Saitual achieved Surakshit status, becoming the first and only district in Mizoram to reach the milestone. Deputy Chief Medical Officer Dr Zothanpari Chhakchhuak credited the achievement to the support of Saitual Deputy Commissioner Srinivas Sadi and close cooperation from community leaders, NGOs and churches, particularly in promoting HIV testing and awareness campaigns. She stressed the need for continued large-scale testing to ensure people know their HIV status and urged those living with HIV to remain on ART regularly to sustain the district’s progress.

national_raw_news.title: India's first indigenous ocean research vessel launched by GRSE - Morung Express
national_raw_news.content: India's first indigenous ocean research vessel launched by GRSE | MorungExpress | morungexpress.com India's first indigenous ocean research vessel launched by GRSE India's first indigenous ocean research vessel launched by GRSE (Photo: PIB) India 9th September 2026 Kolkata, September 9 (IANS): Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers (GRSE) Ltd, a Navratna Defence Public Sector Undertaking under the Ministry of Defence, launched Sagar Manthan, the Ocean Research Vessel (ORV) for the National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Ministry of Earth Sciences, Government of India, on Wednesday. This is the first ORV of its kind to be built in India. The launch comes barely five months after the keel laying of the vessel, highlighting the shipyard's capability to maintain schedules. Dr Jitendra Singh, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for the Ministry of Science and Technology and Ministry of Earth Sciences, who was supposed to attend the event as chief guest virtually, was unable to do so. He, however, sent a message congratulating both GRSE and NCPOR for the achievement. The Minister also highlighted the important role that the ORV will play in India's deep ocean research once it is delivered in 2028. Dr Srinivasa Kumar Tummala, secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences, was present as the guest of honour at the event at GRSE’s Rishi Bankim Shipyard in Kolkata. In his address, the secretary, who is a renowned oceanographer, spoke on the importance of ocean research for the country's development. "We are also building a Marine Acoustic Research Vessel (ARV) for the Ministry of Defence and two Coastal Research Vessels (CRVs). Till now, we used to say that GRSE has achieved Atmanirbharta in warship building. From now onwards, we can say that GRSE has achieved Atmanirbharta, both in the field of warships and specialised vessels," Cmde P R Hari, IN (Retd), chairman and managing director, GRSE, said. The 89.50 m long, 18.80 m wide ORV will have a gross tonnage of 5,900 tonnes and its speed will be 14 knots at 90 per cent maximum continuous rating (MCR). Once delivered, the ORV will be capable of Underway Swath Multibeam as well as Geophysical Seismic surveys in coastal seas and deep waters at a maximum depth of 6 km. She will also be able to carry out Conductivity, Temperature and Depth (CTD) profiling and water sampling operations such as biological sampling using vertical and horizontal methods through various nets. The research vessel will also effectively carry out surface and deep-sea mooring and data buoy operations, seabed sampling using corers and grabs as well as rock dredging with chain bag dredges. The vessel will also undertake underway atmospheric observations, surface meteorological and current measurements, and collect upper air data. Scientists will be able to carry out analytical work and data processing on board. The ship will also provide training and education to scientists and technicians. national_raw_news.title: Union Minister Prataprao Jadhav calls for accessible, people-centric and quality Ayush services
national_raw_news.content: Union Minister Prataprao Jadhav calls for accessible, people-centric and quality Ayush services Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Union Minister Prataprao Jadhav calls for accessible, people-centric and quality Ayush services ANI | Updated: Sep 09, 2026 15:30 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 9 (ANI): Union Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Ayush and Minister of State, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Prataprao Jadhav , called upon States and Union Territories to strengthen the delivery of accessible, people-centric and quality Ayush services across the country, a release said. He was speaking at the National Workshop on ‘Strengthening the Ayush Ecosystem in States and Union Territories’, organised by NITI Aayog at Kanha Shanti Vanam , Hyderabad , yesterday. The workshop brought together senior officials from the Central Government, more than 30 States and Union Territories, and experts from various organisations to deliberate on strengthening the Ayush ecosystem through shared experiences, best practices and collaborative action. The inaugural session was attended by Prataprao Jadhav as Chief Guest, along with Prof M Srinivas, Member (Health), NITI Aayog , and Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush. In his keynote address, Jadhav emphasised the need for coordinated efforts by the Centre, States and UTs to expand the reach and impact of Ayush systems. He called for greater focus on quality, accessibility and people-centric delivery of Ayush healthcare services to address the evolving health needs of the population. M Srinivas highlighted the importance of technology-integrated and evidence-based approaches to integrative healthcare, with the potential to improve health outcomes in India and beyond. Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha emphasised the pivotal role of States and UTs in strengthening the Ayush ecosystem and ensuring effective implementation and delivery of Ayush services at the grassroots level. The workshop provided a platform for States and UTs to share experiences, best practices and innovative approaches across key areas, including Ayush healthcare delivery, education, research, capacity building and integration with the broader healthcare system. The deliberations reaffirmed the importance of Centre-State collaboration in building a stronger, accessible and people-centric Ayush ecosystem and in advancing the Government’s vision of holistic and integrated healthcare for all. The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has significantly ramped up efforts against the illegal cannabis trade, seizing approximately 740 kg of cannabis and charas throughout the country, according to the Ministry of Finance. This crackdown, involving eight major operations over two weeks, has resulted in 13 arrests under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985. In a notable operation on September 8 near Raipur, officials intercepted two trucks from Vishakhapatnam on Old Dhamtari Road. The search yielded 375.95 kg of cannabis hidden in sacks, leading to the arrest of four individuals and the confiscation of both vehicles. Earlier actions in the Raipur corridor on August 26 saw another truck impounded with 124 kg of cannabis concealed within. Along the Aurangabad–Patna Highway, enforcement encountered resistance on September 5 and 6. After a pursuit, they discovered a hidden cavity in the driver's cabin containing 90 packets of ganja, totaling 140.5 kg. Additional seizures occurred in northern rail and road networks and via international air routes, highlighting the breadth of the agency’s comprehensive anti-trafficking strategy. national_raw_news.title: DRI seizes 740 kg cannabis and charas in pan-India crackdown, 13 arrested - ANI News
national_raw_news.content: DRI seizes 740 kg cannabis and charas in pan-India crackdown, 13 arrested Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर DRI seizes 740 kg cannabis and charas in pan-India crackdown, 13 arrested ANI | Updated: Sep 09, 2026 11:58 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 9 (ANI): The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) seized around 740 kg of cannabis and charas across the country as it intensified its crackdown on illegal cannabis trafficking, leading to the arrest of 13 persons under the provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985. According to the Ministry of Finance, the agency conducted eight major operations over the past fortnight, intercepting illicit consignments transported across road, rail, and air corridors. The total haul comprised 709.6 kg of regular cannabis, 24.5 kg of high-grade hydroponic cannabis, and 5 kg of charas. In the latest operation on September 8, enforcement officers intercepted two trucks arriving from Vishakhapatnam at Old Dhamtari Road near Raipur. A vehicle search uncovered 61 packets of cannabis concealed inside 10 sacks in the cargo hold. Officials confiscated 375.95 kg of the narcotic substance along with both vehicles, arresting four individuals at the scene. The Raipur corridor witnessed earlier enforcement action on August 26, when authorities impounded a truck and confiscated approximately 124 kg of concealed cannabis, arresting one suspect. Interceptions on highway networks also encountered resistance. During an operation between September 5 and September 6, agency personnel chased and stopped a truck along the Aurangabad–Patna Highway near Patna. The occupants attacked the intercepting team, injuring one officer, while the driver escaped. A subsequent vehicle search revealed a concealed cavity situated directly behind the driver’s cabin. "A search of the vehicle led to the detection of a secret cavity behind the driver’s cabin, from which 90 packets containing ganja were recovered," the Ministry stated, confirming the seizure of 140.5 kg of the drug and the impounding of the transport vehicle. Transit checks extended into northern rail and road networks earlier in the month. Officers rummaged through a car stopped near Ludhiana in Punjab between September 1 and September 2, discovering 67 packets containing around 69 kg of cannabis hidden inside floor cavities, leading to two arrests. On September 3, officials at Gorakhpur Railway Station screened three passengers aboard the general compartment of the Amarnath Express. A physical search yielded 5 kg of charas. Two passengers concealed the substance within knee-cap coverings bound to their thighs beneath their sarees, with initial investigations tracing the contraband back to Nepal. Aviation routes also formed a key conduit in the trafficking chain. Over the last 15 days, officers mounted three separate airport operations across Hyderabad and Bengaluru. Teams intercepted three passengers arriving from international sectors, specifically Hanoi, Vietnam, and Bangkok, Thailand, confiscating 24.6 kg of high-potency cannabis and arresting all three couriers. The Ministry stated that the sustained interdictions reflect the agency's operational focus on curbing narcotics distribution networks exploiting road, rail, and air transit infrastructure nationwide.
